name: Improvised Resonance Slug IRS-11
description:
The IRS-11 is a black market attempt to solve the TCS-11's weapon-specific frequency matching problem by replacing the fixed resonance cavity with an adjustable tuning mechanism. Produced by independent weapons engineers in illicit workshops, the IRS-11 uses a manually adjustable internal resonance cavity that the operator tunes using a frequency matching tool before loading. In theory, this allows a single ammunition type to work in any BRC-6 weapon regardless of the specific unit's resonance calibration.

In practice, the IRS-11's adjustable cavity introduces mechanical complexity that degrades the slug's performance across several parameters. The tuning mechanism adds mass in the wrong places, shifting the slug's center of gravity and reducing accuracy at range. The movable internal components are also prone to vibration-induced misalignment during firing — the very resonance effect that makes the slug effective can shake the tuning mechanism out of calibration between the barrel and the target. Field reports indicate that IRS-11 slugs achieve approximately 60% of the TCS-11's resonance fracture effect at best, with a catastrophic failure rate of approximately 8% where the slug's internal mechanism fragments in the barrel.

Despite these limitations, the IRS-11 fills a real market need. Operators who obtain BRC-6 weapons through irregular channels — theft, battlefield recovery, black market purchase — cannot get weapon-specific TCS-11 ammunition without Arcturus Defense Solutions' cooperation. The IRS-11 gives these operators a functional, if degraded, ammunition option. The 8% failure rate is accepted as a cost of operating outside the legitimate supply chain.
legality: Prohibited — modified military ammunition, unlicensed manufacturing
specifications:
weight_per_round: 32g (heavier than TCS-11 due to tuning mechanism)
muzzle_velocity: 650 m/s (reduced from 680)
penetration_rating: ~60% of TCS-11 resonance effect
effective_against: Hard armor (degraded), reinforced structures (degraded)
countermeasures: Same as TCS-11 plus the slug's own unreliability
hazard: 8% catastrophic barrel failure rate
variants: IRS-11 Improved (tighter tolerances, 4% failure rate, significantly more expensive)
IRS-11 Fixed (pre-tuned to common BRC-6 calibration frequencies, cheaper but only compatible with specific weapon batches)
cultural_context: The IRS-11 is a testament to the black market's engineering ingenuity and its willingness to accept risk. Every operator who loads an IRS-11 knows the failure statistics and fires anyway, because the alternative is having a BRC-6 with no ammunition. The engineers who produce IRS-11 slugs occupy a respected niche in GLMZ's underground weapons economy — they are problem solvers rather than mere counterfeiters, and the better ones maintain reputations based on their slugs' actual field performance. The IRS-11 Improved variant, with its 4% failure rate, commands prices approaching legitimate TCS-11 ammunition, reflecting the value operators place on not having their weapon explode in their hands.
story_hooks: An IRS-11 slug failed catastrophically during a high-profile operation, killing the operator and leaving forensic evidence at the scene — the slag fragments contain the tuning mechanism's distinctive alloy, which is traceable to a specific black market engineer who is now a person of interest in a military-grade weapons investigation.

A black market engineer claims to have finally achieved 0% failure rate on an IRS-11 variant by incorporating a stolen Arcturus resonance calibration chip — the chip was taken from an Arcturus field service kit, and Arcturus wants it back along with everything the engineer learned from it.
